---
title: "Contacts Start Worker qualification"
description: "Build, verify and hand off the Contacts Worker for controlled Cloudflare cutover."
updatedAt: "2026-11-20"
audience: developers
---

Vercel is the Contacts production origin while publication is held in
`tuturuuu.ci.ts`. The Contacts native workflow qualifies a route-free production
artifact for `tuturuuu-contacts`. It has no provider credentials or publish job.
The hold also freezes new Vercel Contacts deployments.

## Routes and ownership

The [staging candidate census](/build/devops/contacts-start-candidate) from
[run 43805055297](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/actions/runs/43805055297)
records 40 App Router pages, 87 API routes, two Web rewrites, a Web API fallback,
a workspace redirect, a static asset and the candidate probe. The native
registries cover the app's current pages and route handlers and are checked
against the source tree in CI.

Contacts serves tutoring, student and group reports, periodic reports, and local
feedback and auth handlers on both the subdomain and the `/contacts` mount. Web
owns workspace invitations, permission settings, workspace billing, and the
contact billing API at `/api/v1/workspaces/[wsId]/users/[userId]/billing`. The
Contacts router retains the method-specific topic announcement split in its
proxy. Contact billing and account-link APIs follow their existing Web release
process.

The apex mount consumes the central session with request-local authorization.
The bridge limits mounted cookies to the locale and shared access identity,
strips provider refresh tokens, and scopes locale writes to `/contacts`. App
session mint and refresh endpoints return 409 on the mount. The native runtime
keeps build identity behind the existing Contacts API guard.

## Build and artifact

The `Contacts Cloudflare Source` workflow stamps and builds the exact checkout
with the production public Supabase URL and publishable key. It checks the
route registries, app tests, native types and formatting, validates the emitted
configuration, and executes the same dual-host workerd suite on the build and
a fresh restore. Take `contacts-native-<40-character SHA>` only from a run whose
restore job passed. Compare the SHA-256 of the downloaded GitHub artifact ZIP
with the artifact digest recorded by the producing run. Use the sealed receipt
inside `native.tar.gz` to verify the source SHA, config path and file hashes
with the Contacts restore helper before handing off the artifact.

The emitted config owns the worker-first `ASSETS` binding. Qualification
requires explicit `workers_dev: false` and `preview_urls: false`. The config
allowlist rejects routes and custom domains. CI exercises this contract in the
Contacts artifact regression suite and validates it on the emitted and restored
configurations.

Hosted signed-in acceptance is pending an isolated staging profile or an
equivalent private routing setup for both mappings. The native preview selector
changes the permitted Supabase input while the build pins production Web and
issuer origins. The Worker admits the two production hosts. Before any staging
upload, the release owner must verify isolation for the Supabase project, Web
API and auth issuer and approve a private access path for both mappings.

Confirm in the selected Cloudflare account that workers.dev and preview URLs
are disabled and the Worker has zero routes and custom domains. These checks
cover provider settings outside the sealed config. CI runs the original and
restored artifacts in local workerd with fixture egress. The pinned Wrangler
validation adapter stays in place until the
[cf parity gate](/build/development-tools/cf-cli-wrangler-parity) proves
equivalent handling of Void's emitted artifact.

At runtime, configure `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` for the same project as the build and
supply `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` and `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` through the
Worker secret store. Verify they match the intended tier and coordinate the
app-session signing key with the issuer. Those four bindings are required:
without any of them the Worker answers 503 before loading routes.
`UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` and `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` are optional. Without
them the API proxy rate limit fails open, as in Chat, the edge abuse guard
still applies, and the Worker logs one warning per isolate naming the missing
bindings. Provision an Upstash store to restore the per-app proxy limit.
The route table and central API
origin come from the sealed production profile. The Worker has no scheduled
triggers, queues, storage bindings or app-origin retry loop.

## Signed-in acceptance plan

Use the fleet's disposable Contacts identity and an isolated workspace with
tutoring, reports and billing read access. Run the checks against an admitted
native staging target before cutover and repeat them immediately after the
flip on the subdomain and apex mount. Use a second member without the relevant
workspace permissions as a negative control. Capture the source SHA and
`x-tuturuuu-runtime: native` from the admitted deployment.

| Surface | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Session | Sign in through Web, reload a deep link, check session refresh and the required MFA path. On the apex, reuse the Web session and inspect responses for app-session or Supabase cookie writes. Read the exact SHA from the guarded `/api/build-info`. |
| Locale | Open each primary page in EN and VI, reload it, and verify titles, navigation and browser hydration. Explicit locale paths retain the query on the canonical redirect. |
| Tutoring | Open `/[wsId]/users/tutoring`, load the seeded sessions, open the fixture session and verify permission-gated controls. Confirm a member without tutoring access cannot read the same workspace data. |
| Billing | Open the fixture contact's Billing & Growth tab in `/[wsId]/users/database/[userId]`. Check the Web-owned read through both ingress paths and the redirect from `/[wsId]/billing` to the Web billing page. |
| Reports | Open `/[wsId]/users/reports`, a seeded report detail and `/[wsId]/reports`. Compare the report, status and preview with the fixture baseline. Verify that unauthorized reads fail. |

Use seeded reads and previews during cutover smoke. Keep credentials, raw
cookies and customer identifiers out of the evidence. Record host, locale,
source, route, request status and outcome in the private release receipt signed
by the fleet operator. Feature writes with external effects require a separate
disposable acceptance run.

## Cutover checklist

Complete this checklist in the private release record. Canonical traffic changes
require the release owner's approval and the native migration cutover PR.

1. **Identify the release.** Record the accepted main SHA, qualification run,
   original and restore results, sealed archive digest, and the Cloudflare
   account, zone and immutable Worker version. Match the sealed public-input
   digest to the authorized tier. Record the bindings and secret names, staging
   acceptance receipt, operator, and rollback owner.
2. **Capture both ingress mappings.** Export the live Contacts Vercel domain
   mapping and immutable deployment ID, URL and source SHA. Capture DNS,
   proxy/TLS settings and TTLs for the subdomain, and the current Gateway
   config revision and route precedence for the apex mount. Record the live
   response on each ingress before preparing replacement routing.

   | Ingress | Cutover mapping | Recorded rollback target |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | `https://contacts.tuturuuu.com/*` | Send the request to the accepted Contacts version at the original host and path. | Restore the captured subdomain routing to the retained Vercel origin. |
   | `https://tuturuuu.com/contacts` and `/contacts/*` | Route through Gateway to the same Contacts version with the original host and mount prefix. | Restore the captured Gateway revision and its existing mount behavior. |

   Confirm the apex mapping uses segment boundaries and preserves the raw
   query. Keep Web-owned API and page destinations on Web.
3. **Rehearse rollback before admission.** Prove the immutable Vercel
   deployment still answers. In the private environment, apply equivalent
   test mappings for both ingress paths, run the signed-in smoke checks,
   then execute the prepared one-step rollback. Verify that it restores the
   subdomain fallback and the prior apex mount behavior, including login
   callbacks, a tutoring deep link and a Web-owned API read. Record the
   before/after route revisions, source identity, results and elapsed time,
   along with the exact command or API call the rollback owner will execute.
4. **Switch the admitted routing.** After hosted acceptance and approval,
   apply only the two recorded mappings. Repeat the signed-in checks on
   both paths and verify the exact source SHA and the expected runtime
   header. Watch authentication, errors and latency for 30–60 minutes.
5. **Restore on regression.** Use the rehearsed action on a failed
   acceptance check, authentication loop, or material error/latency
   regression. Verify both ingress paths against the captured baseline.
   Keep the prior Vercel deployment and Gateway revision through one
   release cycle. Rollback restores routing without rebuilding or
   modifying application data.

See the [native migration runbook](/build/devops/native-start-migration#rollback).
